venue.heading: Sede e Location
venue.intro: Unisciti a noi al cuore dell'innovazione per DevFest Roma. Trova tutti i dettagli necessari per raggiungere la sede e orientarti comodamente.

directions.publicTransport: La sede è facilmente raggiungibile con i mezzi pubblici. Prendi la Metro B direzione Laurentina e scendi alla fermata Basilica San Paolo, a circa 10 minuti a piedi dalla sede. Dalla fermata Basilica San Paolo partono anche gli autobus 128 o 766: scendi alla prima fermata, attraversa viale Marconi e cammina per 50 metri verso sinistra. Da Roma Termini, prendi la Metro B direzione Laurentina. Dall'aeroporto, raggiungi la stazione Ostiense e prendi la Metro B direzione Laurentina, scendendo a Basilica San Paolo.
directions.parking: Non è disponibile un parcheggio dedicato all'evento. Nelle vicinanze si può trovare parcheggio limitato su strada. Si consiglia vivamente il car pooling o l'uso dei mezzi pubblici.

accessibility.info: I dettagli sull'accessibilità della sede verranno confermati più vicino alla data dell'evento.

about.aboutDescription: La nostra missione è riunire gli sviluppatori locali per imparare, condividere e connettersi attraverso le tecnologie Google e gli eventi guidati dalla community. DevFest è una conferenza globale decentralizzata ospitata dai Google Developer Group.

about.value_innovation_description: Scopri le ultime novità in AI, Cloud, Mobile e Web direttamente dagli esperti Google.
about.value_community_description: Unisciti a migliaia di sviluppatori in un ambiente fondato sulla collaborazione e la crescita reciproca.
about.value_globalImpact_description: Fai parte del più grande evento della community di sviluppatori al mondo, che raggiunge oltre 100 paesi.

ed5cdb60-eb09-49bc-af9c-a1df24e0c921.bioShort:
With over 20 years in the tech industry, Adi is an expert at the intersection of AI, tech startups, and entrepreneurship. Her work is centered on helping startups build successful products and grow, always maintaining a deep focus on the humans behind the users​.

Expertise & Impact:
Driving Startup Success: For 15 years, Adi has served as a Google Developer Expert (GDE) in AI and a Google Accelerator Mentor, where she guides founders in transforming complex AI capabilities into scalable, market-ready products.

Teaching the Next Generation: At Reichman University’s Entrepreneurship School, she teaches Product and AI, dedicated to helping the next generation of entrepreneurs build the skills they need to launch and lead in the tech world.

Humanizing the Tech Space: Through her podcast, "AI & Humans" (Spotify/YouTube), she explores how technology can better serve people, a philosophy she brings to every product she touches.

A Multi-Faceted Life: Adi balances her tech-driven career with a busy home life—she is a mother of four kids, four cats, and a dog, keeping her grounded in the real world.

The Big Picture: Adi combines two decades of high-level experience in AI and product design to help startups scale efficiently while keeping their products human-centered and impactful.

55c6b59b-448d-4e3b-a013-3b23810b6fcd.bioShort:
Daniel is an AI Architect at Payoneer with over two decades of experience leading development teams, both in Israel and abroad, from idea to production. His current focus is AI infrastructure and multi-agent systems in real-world use — the layer that ties together developer tools, knowledge graphs, and product delivery. 

Daniel is a public speaker and a blog writer, and an active contributor to open source. He also runs the "NG-Heroes" meetup, a space for the local tech community to meet and share what they're learning. Outside of work, family comes first. He proudly holds the title of "The Best Developer in the World" — awarded by his wife, and he has no plans to give it back.

Hi, I'm Francesco, based in Rome, Italy. I'm a Computer Scientist, and from 2017 to 2020, I contributed to the European Space Agency's Copernicus project.

I'm an active presence in online developer communities, especially on Twitter, YouTube, and Discord. Recognized as a Docker Captain, I've hosted official Docker events and appeared on their YouTube channel. Professionally, I focus on roles within developer relations, centered around content strategy and community engagement.

Currently, my main creative efforts are directed towards my YouTube channel, where I've interviewed over 250 developers. My content primarily covers Rust, Blockchain technologies, DevOps practices, and Web Development. I also enjoy engaging with the community through live streams

5a25ee5f-9a7b-44e4-9ea6-f70f5ba36244.bioShort:
Giacomo Sergio vanta 25 anni di esperienza nel settore IT. Dopo la laurea in Ingegneria e un'esperienza presso il Consorzio Pisa Ricerche, si trasferisce a Vienna per lavorare come sviluppatore software in ambito finanziario. Nel 2008 fonda Wondersys, guidandone la crescita fino a farla diventare un'azienda internazionale con oltre 20 dipendenti che fornisce soluzioni IT innovative.
Come padre di una bambina con sindrome di Down, sviluppa un profondo interesse per l'uso della tecnologia a supporto dell'inclusione. Questo lo porta a co-fondare YouDoTools Srl, startup innovativa di cui è CTO, con la missione di sviluppare soluzioni software dedicate all'autonomia delle persone con disabilità intellettiva. Grande appassionato di Intelligenza Artificiale, ne guida e promuove l'integrazione nei prodotti dell'azienda per trasformare l'innovazione tecnologica in impatto sociale concreto.

ac1ea296-0d75-4be5-97e3-58c67b792f64.bioShort:
🇮🇹 Con oltre 10 anni di esperienza tra consulenza e aziende digitali, oggi ricopre il ruolo di Experience Strategy & Service Designer Manager presso uno dei principali gruppi italiani di logistica, spedizioni, pagamenti e servizi finanziari dove si occupa di progettare e innovare servizi con l’obiettivo di migliorare concretamente l’esperienza e la vita delle persone. È Ambassador di SheTech, organizzazione non profit impegnata a promuovere la parità di genere nel mondo tech e digital attraverso networking, formazione e sensibilizzazione, contribuendo a creare nuove opportunità e ad abbattere stereotipi e barriere di accesso al settore. Ha inoltre collaborato per diversi anni con l’Università di Roma Tre come assistente di cattedra e cultore della materia nell’ambito della Comunicazione d’impresa, affiancando alla propria esperienza professionale un forte interesse per la formazione e la condivisione delle competenze. È membro della community delle Unstoppable Women di StartupItalia, una rete dedicata a valorizzare il talento e l’imprenditorialità femminile.

🇬🇧 With over 10 years of experience across consulting and digital companies, she currently works as Experience Strategy & Service Designer Manager at one of Italy’s leading groups in logistics, shipping, payments, and financial services, where she focuses on designing and innovating services with the goal of making a tangible difference to people’s experiences and lives. She is an Ambassador for SheTech, a non-profit organization committed to promoting gender equality in the tech and digital sectors through networking, training, and awareness-raising, helping to create new opportunities and break down stereotypes and barriers to entering the industry. She also collaborated for several years with Roma Tre University as a teaching assistant and subject-matter expert in Corporate Communication, combining her professional experience with a strong interest in education and knowledge sharing. She is a member of StartupItalia’s Unstoppable Women community, a network dedicated to promoting female talent and entrepreneurship.

16271985-149a-411d-bebb-e9704df38154.bioShort:
Haim Michael is the Founder and CEO of Zindell Technologies, a company focused on advancing software development in the AI era. With more than 20 years of hands-on experience, he operates at the intersection of software engineering, architecture, and artificial intelligence, helping organizations rethink how modern systems are designed and built.

Haim has led initiatives across enterprise environments, academia, and global developer communities, bringing a pragmatic yet forward-looking approach to technology adoption. His work emphasizes structured, specification-driven development as a foundation for building reliable, scalable, and AI-integrated systems.

In parallel to his executive role, Haim has delivered training and strategic guidance to leading technology companies and has lectured at top academic institutions, including Bar-Ilan University, HIT, Shenkar, and the Technion. He is recognized for staying at the forefront of software development practices, continuously translating emerging capabilities, particularly in AI, into actionable engineering and business value.

featured.about: Charlie è una Staff Engineer presso Uber, dove guida il team dell'infrastruttura per le performance web. Con oltre 12 anni di esperienza nel settore, è una sostenitrice convinta dei pattern web accessibili e dell'architettura CSS moderna. Contribuisce spesso a progetti open-source e ama costruire strumenti che semplificano la vita degli sviluppatori.

1272029.title: WebMCP in Practice: Shipping MCP Servers in the Browser
1272029.abstract:
Every MCP tutorial puts the server on a server. It doesn't have to be there.
If your app already holds the data, the auth, and the UI state, why copy all of it to a backend just so an agent can reach it? WebMCP lets your page expose its own tools to the agent directly, right where the user already is

In this hands-on workshop we'll build WebMCP tools from scratch in TypeScript and ship them inside a real web app. My production deployment is the reference case study: the architectural decisions, the gotchas, and the parts the docs don't cover yet.

You'll leave with working WebMCP tools, a clear sense of when browser-native beats server-side, and patterns you can deploy in your own app on Monday.

1273464.title: One-Person Unicorn: The New Era of Entrepreneurship in the Age of AI
1273464.abstract:
AI is changing startups! Learn how solo founders can build "unicorn" companies faster & leaner, like Bolt & Lovable. This workshop/talk reveals how AI accelerates growth, streamlines development, and redefines entrepreneurial models for rapid success. Get practical tools to launch & scale your business in the new AI era.
3 Main Takeaways: One-Person Unicorn Talk
A. AI as Your Co-Founder: Building Faster with Less
Learn how AI tools can replace entire teams in the early stages - from coding and design to marketing and customer support. Discover the specific AI stack that enables solo founders to build and iterate at unprecedented speed, turning months of development into weeks.
B. The New Lean Startup Model: Validate and Scale Smarter
Understand how AI accelerates the build-measure-learn cycle, allowing you to test ideas with minimal resources and maximum precision. Get practical frameworks for using AI to analyze market feedback, optimize product-market fit, and make data-driven decisions that traditionally required large teams.
C. From Solo to Unicorn: The Strategic Roadmap
Walk away with a concrete action plan for leveraging AI to scale your business without proportionally scaling your team. Learn the key inflection points where AI can 10x your output and the specific tools and strategies that companies like Bolt and Lovable used to achieve massive growth with minimal human resources.

1273802.title: Who Judges the Judge? LLM-as-a-Judge per la qualità dei sistemi GenAI
1273802.abstract:
Creare un prototipo basato su LLM o sistemi RAG oggi è semplice. Il vero problema arriva quando l’applicazione entra in produzione: come possiamo monitorare in modo continuo, scalabile e affidabile la qualità delle risposte, senza dipendere da costosi cicli di validazione manuale?
In questo talk esploriamo il pattern architetturale LLM-as-a-Judge dal punto di vista del Data Engineer: come progettare una pipeline asincrona per raccogliere i log delle interazioni, valutare la qualità degli output e intercettare in tempo quasi reale errori, allucinazioni e risposte irrilevanti. Vedremo come usare metriche come Faithfulness e Context Precision, con framework open-source come Ragas, per costruire un sistema di osservabilità della qualità davvero utile in produzione.

1275223.title: Orchestrating AI Agents in Spec-Driven Development with Kiro IDE
1275223.abstract:
Spec-Driven Development (SDD) fundamentally changes how software is conceived, implemented, and evolved—especially in an era where AI agents are no longer passive assistants, but active collaborators. In this talk, I will share my hands-on experience implementing Spec-Driven Development using Amazon’s Kiro IDE, focusing on how AI agents are orchestrated throughout the development lifecycle to deliver production-ready software with clarity, traceability, and speed.

The session is grounded in real projects in which the Kiro IDE was used to drive development from explicit specifications rather than ad hoc prompts or informal requirements. I will demonstrate how structured specifications—written upfront and continuously refined—become the single source of truth that guides implementation, validation, documentation, and testing. Rather than “coding first and fixing later,” the workflow ensures that what we build consistently matches what we intended to build.

A central theme of the talk is agent orchestration. I will show how Kiro IDE enables developers to define and integrate custom AI agents directly into the IDE, each with a focused responsibility. Examples include agents that autonomously:

Generate and evolve automated tests based on specifications

Produce and maintain technical documentation aligned with the current spec.

Validate implementation decisions against the original requirements.

Assist with controlled refactoring while preserving spec compliance.

The audience will see that creating new agents is far simpler than commonly assumed. I will walk through the process of defining new hooks that lead to new autonomous agents running in our IDE in accordance with the specifications. These agents operate as first-class citizens inside the IDE, collaborating with both the developer and other agents.

The talk also provides a concise yet comprehensive overview of the Spec-Driven Development cycle as implemented in the Kiro IDE. This includes:

Translating intent into structured, machine-readable specifications

Using the spec as a steering document for agent behavior

Iterative implementation guided by continuous spec validation

Automatic generation of tests and documentation as part of the same flow

Maintaining long-term alignment between requirements, code, and artifacts

What makes this workflow unique is not just the use of AI, but the discipline imposed by the spec itself. AI agents are not free-form code generators; they are constrained, directed, and evaluated through explicit specifications. This results in systems that are easier to reason about, review, and evolve—especially in teams and long-lived codebases.

This session is aimed at developers, architects, and engineering leaders who want to move beyond prompt-driven coding toward a more reliable, scalable, and auditable development model. Attendees will leave with a clear mental model of agent orchestration in an IDE, practical examples they can apply immediately, and a deeper understanding of why Spec-Driven Development is emerging as a cornerstone methodology in the AI era.

1278573.title: Hey Google, I want to use AI in my Android App but I'm poor. What are my options?
1278573.abstract:
Everyone wants to build "AI-powered" apps, but few talk about the invoice that arrives at the end of the month. If you are launching a side project or running an indie studio, sustaining a cloud infrastructure for LLMs or image generation is often impossible.

In this session, we shift the focus from the cloud to the device. We will explore the current state of local AI models for Android, walking through the installation and integration of on-device functionality using real-world examples. 

We will also have a glance at what future reserves for us.

1284873.title: AI and accessibility
1284873.abstract: Can AI become a reliable accessibility engineer? Large language models are already an inherent part of modern development workflows but can it also take care of accessibility – from generating semantic HTML and ARIA patterns to reviewing WCAG and EN 301 549 conformance? This talk explores how client-side AI, conversational interfaces, AI skills, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers enable LLMs to interact with browsers, testing frameworks, and accessibility tooling. Through practical examples using axe-core, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, Playwright, and CI/CD pipelines, we will examine how AI can automate parts of accessibility engineering and where it still falls short.

1286351.title: Small LLM in your Browser, - Huge Opportunities for Web Applications
1286351.abstract:
Let's see how AI is becoming a first-class citizen in your browser! In this session, I'll show you Chrome’s Built-In AI APIs - now available behind feature flags in regular Chrome and evolving in Canary. From language detection to summarization and even creative writing, these APIs promise to revolutionize how we build web applications.
Whether you're a developer, tech enthusiast, or decision-maker, this talk will equip you with insights and inspiration to stay ahead in the fast-moving AI landscape.

1286980.title: Antigravity CLI and Flutter: From Prototype to MVP with Gemini
1286980.abstract:
From Idea to App in Minutes: Stop writing boilerplate and start building. Learn how to use the Antigravity CLI and Gemini 3.5 Flash (The most powerful LLM from Google) to turn your prompts into a fully working Flutter MVP without ever leaving your terminal.

But this is more than just code generation. In this session, we will explore the power of "AI Agents" and Model Context Protocols (MCPs). You will discover how these technologies bridge the gap between a simple chat interface and your actual file system, allowing the AI to understand your project structure, run commands, and collaborate with you like a real pair programmer.

1287833.title: From Cloud to Local: Running a Legal Research Agent on Gemma 4
1287833.abstract:
AI agents perform best when backed by a robust architecture that minimizes the model's cognitive load. But is it possible to break free from expensive commercial LLMs for complex tasks like legal research and run the entire system on local hardware?

In this technical talk, we will walk through a practical experiment: how we took the pipeline of Marcus—an agentic RAG pilot for legal research in Latin America originally powered by Gemini and Claude—and pushed its limits by porting it to Gemma 4 using the Agent Development Kit (ADK) on a consumer gaming GPU (RTX 4070 Ti Super 16GB).

We will analyze the engineering shifts required to make an open-weights model run at a commercial-grade level: strict prompt structuring, token budget optimization, and local evaluation strategies.

You will walk away with real-world benchmark results, the formatting hurdles we faced, and a clear roadmap if you are looking to migrate your agentic prototypes to local open-weights environments.

1289815.title: Why Go and LLMs are the perfect match
1289815.abstract:
When we think of Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models (LLMs), our minds automatically jump to Python. But what happens when the model is already trained, and what you actually need is to build massive, fast, and efficient production software around it?

That is where the game changes completely, and where Go (Golang) steps in as the ultimate unsung hero. In fact, key tools in the local AI ecosystem (like Ollama) are written in Go for a very good reason.

In this talk, we will open up the bonnet of modern AI applications to see why the software engineering surrounding the LLM matters just as much as the model itself. We’ll discover how Go’s native concurrency (goroutines and channels) provides the perfect architecture to coordinate complex AI workflows, handle real-time token streaming, and deploy autonomous agents without devouring your servers' memory.

1292196.title: Si fa presto a dire embedding
1292196.abstract:
Ormai sono considerati una sorta di pre-processing per i transformer, ma gli embedding, apparsi quasi quindici anni fa, ne costituiscono la parte essenziale: infatti forniscono il dato numerico, l'unico che un transformer, come una qualsiasi altra rete neurale, sia in grado di manipolare.

Quando ci spiegano come un LLM "vede" il mondo, di solito ci parlano di vettori, distanze del coseno (che poi distanze non sono) e altre nozioni di base che si insegnano da decenni in tutti i corsi di geometria delle facoltà scientifiche.

Ma la grande trovata cartesiana di algebrizzare la geometria scrivendo coordinate per i punti ed equazioni per curve e superficie collima con la nostra intuizione solo in dimensione 2 e 3. Cosa succede in uno spazio con 1000 dimensioni, come quelli dove vivono i vettori usati dai transformer?

La risposta potrebbe sorprendervi

1292641.title: Build Agent Workflows with Gemini, LangChain and LangGraph
1292641.abstract:
This hands-on workshop explores building AI agents, progressing from basic Gemini API prompting to advanced autonomous workflows with LangChain and LangGraph. Participants will gain practical experience using Gemini and these powerful tools to create increasingly capable agents for automating development and engineering tasks. No prior AI agent experience is required – just come ready to code and learn.

Workshop Agenda:
1. Introduction to AI Agents and Gemini API Prompting
2. Building Prompt Chains with LangChain
3. Constructing Autonomous Agents with LangGraph

1293694.title: L'Intelligenza artificiale come strumento di supporto per le persone con disabilità intellettiva
1293694.abstract:
L'Intelligenza Artificiale viene spesso celebrata per la sua capacità di ottimizzare processi industriali o generare contenuti creativi. Ma cosa succede quando mettiamo questa straordinaria potenza al servizio della fragilità e dell'inclusione?

Per una persona con disabilità intellettiva e per la sua intera rete (famiglia, scuola, clinici e associazioni), l'AI smette di essere un semplice trend tecnologico per diventare uno strumento in grado di abilitare un diritto fondamentale: l'autodeterminazione. 

L'intelligenza artificiale può essere un valido supporto per la persona con disabilità intellettiva così come per tutta la rete di persone che le ruotano attorno (caregiver e familiari, operatori, medici, insegnanti, ecc.). Inoltre, l'uso dei Large Language Models, permettendo la traduzione automatica di testi complessi (leggi, contratti, manuali) in formati Easy-to-Read (facili da leggere e da capire), garantisce il diritto all'informazione e la democratizzazione dei contenuti azzerando l'isolamento culturale e permette di costruire applicazioni più accessibili.

In questo talk, partendo dalla mia doppia prospettiva di ingegnere e padre di una bambina con Sindrome di Down, esploreremo come trasformare l'IA da semplice oracolo ad assistente specializzato per la vita indipendente, analizzando le potenzialità della tecnologia in due ambiti chiave:

1. Costruzione di una "memoria sicura" (RAG Engine e Google ADK)
L'utilizzo di sistemi RAG per la creazione di database di conoscenza al servizio di persone con disabilità intellettiva, caregiver e operatori. Vedremo come l'AI possa elaborare in modo sicuro la documentazione clinica, pedagogica e normativa per offrire risposte verificate, aiutando terapisti e famiglie. Inoltre, esploreremo come rendere accessibili materiali provenienti dal mondo della ricerca, fornendo una visione chiara sui progressi scientifici in diversi ambiti.

2. Autonomia nella Vita Quotidiana
Lo sviluppo di agenti autonomi capaci di semplificare la complessità quotidiana fungendo da assistenti personali. L'obiettivo è dare alle persone con disabilità intellettiva quel piccolo aiuto in più che permetta una vita più autonoma e, al contempo, diminuisca il carico cognitivo e fisico sui caregiver.

Siamo di fronte ad un bivio: inclusione radicale o un nuovo e più grande digital divide?
Affrontare oggi questo tema non è opzionale. Infatti, ignorare l'accessibilità cognitiva nello sviluppo dei futuri sistemi di Intelligenza Artificiale rischia di creare un divario sociale ed economico ancora maggiore, escludendo definitivamente le persone più fragili da un mondo sempre più automatizzato. Al contrario, bilanciare la conformità all'AI Act con la necessità di dataset specifici e inclusivi è l'unica via per una vera democratizzazione tecnologica. La sfida che abbiamo davanti non è semplicemente tecnologica, ma profondamente culturale ed etica. L'AI può aprirci porte straordinarie, ma la direzione dobbiamo sceglierla noi: il mio invito è quello di concentrare le nostre energie, la nostra sensibilità e le nostre intelligenze umane verso un unico obiettivo comune, che è poi l'unico che conta davvero: la costruzione di un mondo migliore, più equo e che non lasci indietro nessuno.

1293747.title: Building a Secure Web Architecture on Google Cloud: From Landing Zone to Production-Ready Patterns
1293747.abstract:
In this talk, I walk through the practical journey of building a secure web architecture on Google Cloud, starting from the cloud foundation: organization setup, billing, IAM groups, folders, budgets, and networking. From there, we evolve a simple web app into a production-style architecture using private Compute Engine VMs, IAP, Cloud NAT, managed instance groups, health checks, an external Application Load Balancer, DNS, HTTPS, Cloud Armor, rolling updates, rollback, and autoscaling.
The focus is not only on which services to use, but why each layer exists, what tradeoff it solves, and how to explain these choices clearly to engineers and stakeholders.

1298641.title: ~2 Bits of (in)Confidence
1298641.abstract: A journey through information entropy, LLM compression, and the mathematics of intelligence, assembled with the help of a system that stores approximately 2 bits of real information per parameter and confidently presents all the rest. What could possibly go wrong?

1299834.title: AI, fatti i dati tuoi! Proteggere strumenti e flussi dagli errori a cascata degli agenti autonomi
1299834.abstract: Come proteggere i flussi aziendali quando gli agenti AI prendono decisioni autonome e accedono a strumenti critici? Una panoramica di alto livello su come insegnare all'AI a "farsi i dati suoi", isolando i rischi ed evitando che un singolo bug si propaghi a cascata nell'intero sistema.

1300555.title: The Pillars of AI Native Engineering: how to stay relevant as a Software Engineer in the AI age.
1300555.abstract:
"Software Engineers will be replaced by AI": we've heard this sentence so many times. My bet is different: software engineers, supercharged by AI will be even more powerful! 

The usage of AI will become normal, and even old-school engineers will change their ways of working, or will be pushed outside of the market at some point.

After investing hundreds of hours of writing enterprise-grade software, testing tens of fools and approaches, and failing countless times, we're starting to better understand how to leverage AI properly in our job as Software engineers. 

Methodologies like Spec-driven development are emerging, agents generate better results, and humans are starting to work at a different level of abstraction. 

In this talk, we will analyze how AI is changing the way we develop software, and how we can stay relevant and bring even more value, in a world where coding agents are faster, cheaper (and sometimes better) than us in writing code.

1302571.title: Architecting Autonomous Run loops: State Machine Design and Execution Patterns with Google Gemini
1302571.abstract:
While integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into simple request-response flows is straightforward, building autonomous agents that can plan, execute tools, and solve complex problems remains a significant engineering hurdle. Unconstrained agent loops are inherently prone to unpredictability, infinite execution loops, and security vulnerabilities. To build reliable, production-grade agents, we must enforce structure on their autonomy.

In this technical session, we will explore how to model agent workflows as deterministic state machines using Google Gemini and Google Cloud. We will break down the architecture of the autonomous run loop (Perceive →→Plan →→Execute →→Observe) and examine how to utilize Gemini’s native structured outputs and function calling to drive reliable state transitions.

Attendees will learn how to design robust execution patterns, establish security boundaries to prevent prompt injections during tool execution, and manage persistent agent state over long-lived sessions. You will walk away with a practical architectural blueprint for balancing probabilistic AI reasoning with deterministic system reliability.

1303081.title: Firebase Fundamentals: Structuring Your NoSQL Data for Scalability and Reporting
1303081.abstract:
Firebase offers a powerful and flexible NoSQL database solution, enabling real-time data synchronization and effortless scalability for your applications. However, designing your data structure for optimal performance and reporting can be challenging. In this session, we'll delve into the fundamentals of Firebase's NoSQL database and explore key principles for effectively structuring your data to achieve scalability while enabling SQL-based reporting capabilities.

We'll cover topics like:

Data Modeling Best Practices: Understand how to model your data in a way that promotes efficient queries and avoids common pitfalls.
Denormalization for Performance: Learn how to strategically denormalize data to optimize read performance and minimize data retrieval costs.
Indexing Strategies: Discover the importance of indexing and how to implement indexes effectively to speed up queries.
SQL Integration for Reporting: Explore strategies for integrating SQL-based reporting tools with your Firebase data, including tips for data transformation and export.
Real-World Examples: Analyze practical examples that illustrate how to apply these principles to real-world Firebase projects.
By the end of this session, you'll have the essential knowledge and strategies to design Firebase data structures that can scale seamlessly with your growing user base and application complexity, while also empowering you to leverage the power of SQL for comprehensive reporting and analytics.

1320557.title: The Era of Doers: Stop Overthinking It, (Please)
1320557.abstract:
Siamo probabilmente in uno dei momenti più interessanti per essere sviluppatori. AI, nuovi strumenti e tecnologie ci permettono di trasformare un'idea in qualcosa di reale più velocemente che mai. Allo stesso tempo, però, non è mai stato così facile perdersi tra nuovi modelli, nuovi tool, opinioni e discussioni su come cambierà il nostro futuro.

Voglio parlare di un approccio diverso: fare come first class citizen.

Sperimentare, costruire qualcosa, sbagliare, imparare e riprovare. Senza aspettare di sentirsi pronti, senza cercare la soluzione perfetta e senza passare troppo tempo a prevedere cosa succederà.

Soprattutto per chi sta iniziando oggi, la capacità più importante non sarà conoscere ogni tecnologia, ma saper imparare, adattarsi velocemente e trasformare le proprie idee in qualcosa di concreto.

Anche in un ecosistema che evolve velocemente come quello di Google e dell'AI, gli strumenti continueranno a cambiare.

La capacità di fare, imparare e adattarsi resterà.

1324803.title: Tutorial sull'agentic loop
1324803.abstract: Impariamo passo per passo come è fatto un agentic loop, cuore di un agente AI.

1343851.title: Più AI, più persone: stereotipi di genere e nuove opportunità nel tech
1343851.abstract:
🇮🇹 L’AI sta cambiando il modo in cui impariamo, scriviamo codice e costruiamo prodotti, abbassando alcune delle barriere che per anni hanno reso l'entrata nel tech più difficile. Ma può davvero aiutarci a rendere il settore più inclusivo? Partendo da esempi concreti, parleremo di AI, stereotipi di genere e nuove opportunità per le ragazze che vogliono avvicinarsi allo sviluppo e alla tecnologia. Perché se oggi possiamo costruire più facilmente, possiamo anche scegliere di costruire un tech in cui più persone possano riconoscersi e trovare il proprio spazio.

LA SESSIONE SI TERRA' IN LINGUA ITALIANA

🇬🇧 AI is changing the way we learn, write code, and build products, lowering some of the barriers that have made entering the tech industry more difficult for years. But can it really help us make the sector more inclusive? Starting from concrete examples, we will talk about AI, gender stereotypes, and new opportunities for girls who want to explore software development and technology. Because if we can build more easily today, we can also choose to build a tech industry where more people can see themselves and find their place.

THE SESSION WILL BE HELD IN ITALIAN

1344585.title: Unicode invisibile: attacchi pratici agli LLM
1344585.abstract: I caratteri Unicode invisibili e gli omoglifi possono aggirare i filtri di sicurezza degli LLM in modi quasi impercettibili. In questo talk mostreremo dal vivo come costruire payload che eludono controlli di input, moderazione e validazione, sfruttando normalizzazione, confusori visivi e edge case Unicode. Analizzeremo esempi concreti di attacchi, tecniche di rilevamento e contromisure a livello di carattere, con demo di codice e best practice per difendersi in contesti reali e accademici.
